citations.quote: right lower‑lobe adenocarcinoma with EGFR exon 19 deletion

candidates.description: The status of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene regarding the presence of activating mutations.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Assign 'mutant' if the text mentions 'EGFR exon 19 deletion' or other activating mutations; assign 'wild-type' if 'EGFR wild-type' is explicitly stated.
candidates.measurement_definition: Categorized as 'mutant' if an activating mutation (e.g., exon 19 deletion) is identified; 'wild-type' if no activating mutation is detected via molecular testing.
candidates.name: EGFR Mutation Status
candidates.uncertainty: It is uncertain whether the specific site of mutation (e.g., exon 19 vs exon 21) provides distinct clinical utility over a binary mutant/wild-type classification.

squamous cell carcinoma of the lung, consistent with prior histology

candidates.description: The histological classification of the non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on pathology.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the histology specified in the pathology or diagnosis section; assign 'adenocarcinoma' or 'squamous cell carcinoma'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Determined via pathology report microscopic description and immunohistochemistry (IHC) markers.
candidates.name: Tumor Histology
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence does not specify how cases of mixed histology or poorly differentiated tumors would be categorized.

limitations: Small number of patients provided in the evidence.
Limited diversity in PD-L1 expression values (all cited cases reported 10%), preventing its use as a meaningful continuous variable.
summary: The provided evidence supports the identification of baseline genomic and histological markers in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), specifically EGFR mutation status and tumor histology, which are consistently documented across the patient cases.
